proposed_handoff_items.text: In the visible /workspace session, main.py was implemented and written successfully. run(value) validates the full input before searching, builds undirected adjacency, and uses heapq with (total minutes, link count, full node tuple) priorities and per-node best values. Results are exactly {"route":[...],"minutes":integer}; unreachable gives {"route":[],"minutes":null}, and from==to gives [from] at zero cost. Route ties prefer fewer links, then ordinary integer-sequence lexicographic order.

Task constraints: Python 3.12 standard library only; main.py is the sole allowed output file. Input must have exactly nodes, links, from, to. nodes is 1..8; endpoints are indices 0..nodes-1. links has at most 28 objects, each containing exactly integer a, b, minutes; a!=b, minutes is 1..100, and unordered endpoint pairs cannot repeat. Booleans are not integers. Reject missing/extra fields at every object level.

Strict parsing was preserved: duplicate-key object hook, parse_float rejection, and parse_constant rejection. Malformed JSON, noninteger JSON number syntax, and schema violations produce exactly {"error":"invalid"}. RecursionError was added to the CLI exception handler for deeply nested input. The CLI reads one JSON value and writes one compact JSON value plus newline, without stdout diagnostics.

Observed validation exited 0: CLI checks asserted exact stdout, empty stderr, and successful exit for normal routes, unreachable/stay cases, all tie-break levels, reversed edges, invalid schemas, duplicate keys, exponent/float syntax, NaN/infinities, and deep nesting. Also passed 400 seeded random graph comparisons against exhaustive simple-path enumeration and an eight-node complete-graph case.

Scoped execution constraints in that session: isolated networkless guest, POSIX sh and python, no apply_patch or dependency installation. Python pathlib editing and subprocess validation worked. Actions used one JSON command/final object; decoded commands were limited to 8192 UTF-8 bytes, 30 seconds, and 16 shared steps. No operational failure was observed.

Booking task: implement main.py/run(value) as a Python 3.12 standard-library CLI, with no dependencies. The current brief/source are authoritative; the supplied source was a fresh canonical starter, not a previous completed submission. Inspect future supplied source rather than assuming the prior implementation persists.

Input must be exactly {"requests":[...]}, with 0..16 requests. Each request has exactly id, start, end, urgency, all integers (not booleans): unique id 1..999, start 0..1439, end start+1..1440, urgency 0..9. Reject missing/extra fields at every object level. Process higher urgency first; equal urgency MUST preserve input order, not sort by ID. One room (0); greedily accept only if the whole half-open interval is free. Adjacent intervals do not conflict; never move/shorten accepted bookings. Output exactly scheduled:[{id,room:0},...] and rejected:[id,...], both sorted by increasing ID and partitioning all requests.

CLI contract: read one strict JSON value from stdin and emit one JSON value on stdout, without diagnostics there. Reject malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, noninteger numeric syntax (including floats/exponents), nonfinite constants, and schema violations with exactly {"error":"invalid"}. The starter uses object_pairs_hook=unique_object, parse_float=invalid, parse_constant=invalid and exact-type validation helpers; preserve strict parsing.

Observed prior work: run() was implemented with complete schema/range/ID validation, stable descending-urgency sorting, pairwise half-open overlap checks, and ID-sorted outputs. RecursionError was added to the CLI exception handler. The edit/test command exited 0: CLI checks covered empty/boundary inputs, input-order ties, adjacency, urgency, malformed/duplicate/noninteger JSON, schema/type/range errors, and deep nesting. Also passed 500 seeded cases against an independent occupied-minute reference, with input nonmutation checked.

Prior guest context stated /workspace, only main.py allowed for submission, networkless execution, POSIX sh and python with standard library, and no apply_patch. Python pathlib reads/writes and subprocess CLI checks actually succeeded there. No operational failure was observed; these observations do not guarantee capabilities in another environment.

retained_pg_facts.text: Booking CLI main.py uses Python 3.12 stdlib only: one JSON stdin/stdout value, no stdout diagnostics. Preserve strict parsing: malformed JSON, duplicate keys, noninteger syntax, booleans as integers and schema errors return exactly {"error":"invalid"}.

Booking input has exactly {"requests":[...]}, 0..16 requests. Each has exactly integer id (1..999, unique), start (0..1439), end (start+1..1440), urgency (0..9); missing or extra fields at every level are invalid.

Booking scheduler has one room (0). Process requests once by descending urgency, preserving input order on ties. Half-open intervals allow end/start adjacency. Accept only fully free intervals; never move or shorten accepted bookings.

Booking output is exactly {"scheduled":[{"id":integer,"room":0},...],"rejected":[integer,...]}; lists partition all requests and sort by id. The milestone's fresh canonical starter was authoritative; complete behavior belongs in run(value).

Booking /workspace guest contract: isolated and networkless; POSIX /bin/sh and python stdlib, no apply_patch or installs. Python file operations or shell redirection were prescribed for edits. Only main.py was allowed output.

Booking guest required exactly one JSON {"command":...} or {"final":...} action: decoded commands <=8192 UTF-8 bytes, 16 total actions, 30s per command. Its contract specified timeout or invalid/oversized response terminated the session without retry.
